ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, given that the graphs of the functions $y=x+b$ and $y=ax+3$ intersect at point $P$, what is the solution set of the inequality $x+b<ax+3$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since the x-coordinate of the intersection point of the two lines is: $x=1$,\\
by examining the graph, it is evident that when $x<1$, $x+b<ax+3$;\\
therefore, the answer is $\boxed{x<1}$.
